A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Agent Security Bench (ASB). Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F are readable and support reliable matching across terminology changes, renumbering, and relocations.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulated-agent experiments across 13 LLM backbones, including attack and defense results in Tables 5–7 and utility, trigger, and detection analyses in Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds pairwise attack-combination experiments, Dynamic Prompt Rewriting evaluations, and derived utility–security scores.

M1.justification: v2 adds Dynamic Prompt Rewriting, which modifies query meaning to prioritize security, task relevance, and contextual consistency, beyond the existing paraphrasing defense (Appendix A.4.1). The ReAct framework and PoT backdoor procedure remain unchanged; OPI becoming IPI is a terminology change.

E1.justification: The same ten domains, 50 agent tasks, 400 attack tasks, and aggressive/non-aggressive categories remain. Table 14 adds two-channel compromise scenarios—DPI+IPI, DPI+memory poisoning, and IPI+memory poisoning—alongside the previously evaluated individual and three-channel attacks. No new dataset or application domain is introduced.

E2.justification: Dynamic Prompt Rewriting joins the evaluated DPI defenses in v2 Table 7 and the clean-utility comparison in Table 19. Table 14 also compares three newly evaluated pairwise attack variants with the existing three-way attack. The 13 backbones and other defense comparators are retained.

E3.justification: v2 introduces NRP as an evaluation metric and adds pairwise-versus-three-way attack comparisons. Separate ASR-d and PNA-d entries are consolidated into ASR and PNA, while defended evaluations remain. The simulated-tool setup, backbone configurations, and PoT demonstration/test-task split are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix D.1.2 adds component comparisons investigating which attack combinations help or interfere. v2 also adds DPR clean-utility controls, analyses relating PNA to attack success and backbone capability, and detailed execution cases for DPI, IPI, memory poisoning, and mixed attacks. Existing trigger and detection-threshold analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates and averages across models or conditions without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. v2 introduces no new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial result entries: Table 14 reports average ASRs of 79.06%, 83.02%, and 23.75% for the three pairwise combinations; Tables 7 and 19 report DPR averages of 44.45% ASR and 26.38% clean-task performance; Table 6 adds NRP rankings. These are additional comparisons, while Table 5 and the matched earlier result columns remain numerically unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 introduces the mathematical definition NRP = PNA × (1 − ASR) in Equation 20. The central attack definitions and PoT objectives remain unchanged, including the mixed-attack equation relocated to Appendix A.1. Added ASR/PNA formulas explain existing metrics; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction add NRP and its proposed use in backbone selection as an explicit contribution, and expand stated coverage from 23 to 27 attack/defense variants. The central ASB and PoT contributions, vulnerability claim, 84.30% headline result, and limited-defense-effectiveness conclusion remain.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands interpretations of attack-combination synergy and interference, NRP-based model selection, and individual defense failures. Appendix D.2 adds proposed defenses and computational or response-time tradeoffs. The new cost-efficiency recommendation and several mechanism explanations extend beyond what the reported measurements directly establish.

D1.justification: Appendix C adds the exact DPR prompt and documents tool-call parsing, schema validation, execution functions, simulation classes, fixed tool outputs, and relevant code/data locations. These clarify the existing implementation rather than establish a changed execution pipeline. AIOS, Chroma, PoT task selection, and repository availability were already documented.

R1.justification: Appendix B.3 and Table 12 expand the comparison with already-cited InjecAgent and AgentDojo. v2 adds references supporting simulated-tool evaluation and recent agent research, and removes the Data-centric NLP Backdoor Defense reference. ASB's established positioning as a broader security benchmark remains.

P1.justification: v2 reorganizes the experimental narrative, moves mixed-attack formalization and detailed attack-result discussion into appendices, and subdivides the implementation and analysis appendices. It expands explanations and examples, standardizes OPI to IPI, and removes the duplicated defense-results paragraph in v1 Section 5.4.

P2.justification: Figure 2 expands from one to three scatterplots. v2 adds NRP, benchmark-comparison, and attack-combination tables, extends two defense tables with DPR columns, and adds execution-transcript boxes. Diagrams are revised, and v1's memory-detection Figure 4 becomes Table 21 with the same numerical content.

improvement.justification: The combination tests, DPR attack/utility comparisons, and clearer execution documentation make v2 more informative and easier to assess than v1. The gains are limited by unvalidated NRP and cost-efficiency interpretations, plus new inconsistencies: Appendix C.2.3 describes BP with a trigger present, contradicting Table 4, and Table 3 retains the old attack count. These issues temper a supported, modest overall improvement.
